image_description: A close-up photograph of a brown butterfly, identified as a ringlet (Aphantopus hyperantus), resting on green vegetation. The wings are held closed, displaying the ventral side which is uniformly brown with a row of distinct eyespots (ocelli) along the margins. The body is slender and hairy, matching the wing coloration. Antennae are visible and appear clubbed. The background consists of blurred green leaves and dry grass stems.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The antennae are clearly visible extending from the head. They exhibit the characteristic thickening at the tips (clubs) typical of butterflies.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall morphology matches that of a satyrid butterfly. While absolute size is hard to judge without a scale, the proportions relative to the leaf suggest a moderate wingspan consistent with the species (30-50mm).

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wings are a uniform matte brown. A clear row of black eyespots with white pupils is visible along the outer margin of both the forewing and hindwing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings held closed at rest revealing cryptic ventral patterning.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The butterfly is perched with wings folded vertically above the body, exposing the underside (ventral) pattern, which is cryptic and matches the description.

The body appears slender relative to the wing size and has a visible fuzzy/hairy texture.
